papers.title: Phenomenology of strangeness-changing two-body currents in antineutrino scattering
papers.abstract: Antineutrinos produce hyperons without kaons through Cabibbo-suppressed quasi-elastic scattering on a single nucleon. A two-body current acting on a correlated nucleon pair, nubar [NN] -> l+ Y N', gives the same hyperons plus a second nucleon. A companion paper constructs this current without fixing its size. StrangeMC, the only generator with the channel, set it to a flat 15% of the quasi-elastic hyperon cross section. We determine the ratio f = sigma_2p2h/sigma_QE of the two-body to the quasi-elastic hyperon cross section on carbon versus antineutrino energy, and the detector signatures of two-body events. The strange two-body current and its non-strange counterpart are computed on the same nucleon pair. Their ratio is converted into f with the Valencia non-strange 2p2h and quasi-elastic cross sections for carbon, assuming that nuclear effects missing from the pair are common to both. Under this assumption f rises from 0.14 at 0.6 GeV to 0.20-0.22 at 2-5 GeV. Averaged over the Booster antineutrino spectra it is 0.15-0.17, close to the 15% placeholder, which StrangeMC now replaces with f(E). The largest evaluated uncertainty comes from separating the two-body current from one-body production followed by rescattering: across the separation prescriptions explored, f at 1 GeV ranges from 0.12 to 0.22. Interference with one-body production is not calculated and could be as large as the two-body rate. In a simulated SBND antineutrino-mode exposure on argon with the carbon f, two-body events are about 11% of events that produce a strange hadron. They supply more than a quarter of the kaon-less Sigma+ events used to tag hyperon charge exchange, partly as Sigma+ made at the weak vertex. They reconstruct 12-30% low in energy under the quasi-elastic hypothesis. After final-state interactions half of them have a proton above 40 MeV at the vertex, against a fifth of quasi-elastic events.
papers.reason: Phenomenological construction and event generator implementation of strangeness-changing two-body current (2p2h) contributions in antineutrino-nucleus scattering, squarely in core research.

summary.tldr: Calculates the strangeness-changing 2p2h antineutrino cross section relative to quasi-elastic hyperon production on carbon and argon, finding a 15-22% contribution that creates substantial low-energy reconstruction bias and affects hyperon charge-exchange tags.
summary.novel_idea: Replaces the flat 15% placeholder used in the StrangeMC generator with a dynamic, energy-dependent ratio $f(E)$ computed via a transfer ansatz linking chiral $|\Delta S|=1$ two-body currents to Valencia $|\Delta S|=0$ 2p2h results. It presents the first detailed phenomenological assessment of how $|\Delta S|=1$ 2p2h currents alter energy reconstruction, vertex proton multiplicities, and hyperon charge-exchange tagging in SBN and DUNE.
summary.method: An $SU(3)$ chiral Lagrangian model generates $|\Delta S|=1$ and mirror $|\Delta S|=0$ two-body currents on correlated nucleon pairs ($p=0.25\text{ GeV}$). The ratio of pair cross sections is normalized to the Valencia non-strange 2p2h carbon calculation. Formation-length and principal-value matching prescriptions separate the 2p2h current from quasi-elastic production followed by intranuclear cascade rescattering within StrangeMC.
key_results: The 2p2h-to-QE hyperon cross-section ratio $f(E)$ on carbon rises from 0.14 at 0.6 GeV to 0.20-0.22 at 2-5 GeV, averaging 0.15-0.17 over Booster antineutrino fluxes.
Quasi-elastic energy reconstruction of 2p2h hyperon events is biased low by 12% at 0.6 GeV, 22% at 1 GeV, and 30% at 3 GeV.
Two-body reactions provide 28% of kaon-less $\Sigma^+$ events at SBND, with primary $\Sigma^+$ produced directly at the weak vertex on $pp$ pairs accounting for 12%.
Current-cascade matching choice yields the largest evaluated uncertainty, shifting $f(1\text{ GeV})$ between 0.12 and 0.22, while uncalculated 1-body/2-body interference could be equally large.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling, 2p2h/meson-exchange currents, event generator physics (GENIE, StrangeMC), and oscillation systematic uncertainties for DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande hyperon samples.
summary.caveats: Interference between one-body production with rescattering and two-body currents is neglected and could be as large as the 2p2h rate itself ($|\rho| \approx 0.2$). Argon values are extrapolated from carbon via scaling ansatz.

papers.title: High significance measurement of reactor coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering on germanium by CONUS+
papers.abstract: We report the most precise measurement to date of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$\nu$NS) from reactor antineutrinos using the CONUS+ high-purity germanium detectors at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant. With an exposure of 1296 kg$\cdot$days reactor-on, a blind likelihood analysis yields $1555 \pm 152$ CE$\nu$NS events, with a significance of 10.2 $\sigma$, in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of $1701 \pm 198$ events within 0.6 standard deviations. The result also determines the weak mixing angle at a momentum transfer of about 10 MeV, $\sin^2\theta_W = 0.225 \pm 0.022$, consistent with the Standard Model prediction.
papers.reason: Reports high-significance reactor CEvNS measurement with HPGe detectors by CONUS+, directly hitting core low-energy neutrino physics.

summary.tldr: CONUS+ reports a 10.2-sigma observation of reactor antineutrino CEvNS on HPGe detectors, measuring 1555 signal events and extracting the weak mixing angle $\sin^2\theta_W = 0.225 \pm 0.022$ at $Q \approx 10\text{ MeV}$.
summary.novel_idea: Achieves the highest significance measurement of reactor CEvNS to date using upgraded 2.42 kg HPGe detectors deployed 20.7 m from the Leibstadt reactor. The upgrade increased active target mass by ~50% and halved the per-unit-mass background level relative to Run 1.
summary.method: Data was collected with three HPGe detectors (5.60 kg total active mass) yielding 1296 kg-days reactor-on exposure. A blind, binned Poisson likelihood fit was executed simultaneously across reactor-on and reactor-off energy spectra from threshold (140-170 eVee) up to 800 eVee using a MaGe/Geant4 background model and Lindhard quenching ($k=0.162 \pm 0.004$).
key_results: Extracted $1555 \pm 152$ CEvNS events ($10.2\sigma$ significance), matching the Standard Model prediction of $1701 \pm 198$ events ($N_s/N_{\mathrm{SM}} = 0.91 \pm 0.14$).
Determined the weak mixing angle $\sin^2\theta_W = 0.225 \pm 0.022$ at momentum transfer $Q \approx 10\text{ MeV}$, consistent with the SM value of 0.2387.
Achieved a total relative signal uncertainty of 9.8% (7.5% statistical, 6.3% systematic).
summary.why_it_matters: Provides high-precision low-energy CEvNS cross-section data on germanium, directly constraining low-energy electroweak parameters, non-standard interactions (NSI), and light BSM mediators.
summary.caveats: The total signal prediction uncertainty (11.6%) remains dominated by threshold energy-scale calibration (8.0%) and the quenching factor (7.5%).

papers.title: Analysis of CONUS+ run 2: Detector performance, background model and CE$\nu$NS measurement
papers.abstract:
Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$
u$NS) provides a uniquely sensitive probe of neutrino properties, but its detection requires pushing energy thresholds to the sub-keV scale while controlling backgrounds. The CONUS+ experiment, located at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant, reported the first observation of CE$
u$NS using reactor antineutrinos in 2025. Following a detector upgrade that replaced three of the original 1 kg high-purity germanium detectors with larger 2.42 kg diodes, this paper presents the analysis of the CONUS+ run 2 dataset, including the detector characterization, the background model, the signal prediction and expected sensitivity, and the extraction of the CE$
u$NS signal. The new detectors reach a background level per unit mass reduced by approximately a factor of two relative to the original detectors, while reaching energy thresholds between 140 and 170 eV$_{ee}$. With an exposure of 1296 kg$\cdot$days reactor-on and 86 kg$\cdot$days reactor-off, a blind likelihood analysis fitting directly the number of signal counts yields $N_s = 1555 \pm 152$ CE$
u$NS events, corresponding to a significance of 10.2$\,\sigma$. The result is in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of $1701 \pm 198$ events, with $N_s/N_{\mathrm{SM}} = 0.91 \pm 0.14$.
papers.reason: Detailed detector performance and background analysis for the CONUS+ reactor CEvNS experiment, a prime interest for low-energy neutrino detection.

summary.tldr: Provides the detailed technical analysis for CONUS+ Run 2, covering HPGe detector upgrades, sub-keV energy calibrations, a MaGe/Geant4 background model, and statistical extraction of 1555 CEvNS events.
summary.novel_idea: Presents comprehensive characterization and performance data for the upgraded CONUS+ 2.42 kg HPGe detectors, including in situ $^{71}\text{Ge}$ sub-keV line calibrations, transition/dead layer modeling, pulse-shape discrimination validation, and an updated likelihood parameterization fitting signal counts directly.
summary.method: Calibrated energy scales down to sub-keV energies using internal $^{71}\text{Ge}$ K-shell (10.37 keVee) and L-shell (1.30 keVee) electron-capture peaks. Simulated cosmic muon/neutron backgrounds using MaGe/Geant4, accounting for reactor drywell lid shielding changes during off-periods, and performed pulse-shape analysis ($A/E$ and risetime) to validate bulk versus surface event models.
key_results: Achieved operational energy thresholds between 140 and 170 eVee with a threshold energy-scale calibration uncertainty of 3 eVee.
Reduced background per unit mass by a factor of ~2 in the new 2.42 kg diodes owing to superior radiopurity and surface-to-volume ratio.
Lowered total systematic uncertainty on the CEvNS signal prediction from 16.4% in Run 1 to 11.6% in Run 2.
summary.why_it_matters: Serves as an operational reference on HPGe performance, sub-keV energy calibration, and background modeling techniques for reactor CEvNS experiments and low-energy dark matter/neutrino detectors.
summary.caveats: Residual surface-event excesses in pulse-shape analysis indicate simplified simulation geometries, though these were verified not to impact the CEvNS region of interest.

papers.title: Search for Neutrino-Produced Long-Lived Particles Using the SBND Cosmic Ray Tagger Beam Telescope
papers.abstract: The Short-Baseline Near Detector (SBND) is a liquid argon time projection chamber in Fermilab's Short-Baseline Neutrino Program, positioned 110 meters from the neutrino target along the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB). In addition to its neutrino physics goals, SBND enables searches for new physics, including long-lived particles (LLPs) produced via neutrino-nucleus upscattering that decay into visible final states. Although neutrino data taking with the full SBND experiment began in December 2024, a subset of the Cosmic Ray Tagger (CRT) system operated from 2017--2018 as a standalone detector, referred to as the CRT Beam Telescope, collecting data corresponding to $2.95\times 10^{20}$ protons on target from the BNB. Originally intended for commissioning and performance studies, the substantial dataset collected also enables searches for displaced LLP decays. This paper presents the first search for physics beyond the Standard Model using data from the SBND CRT Beam Telescope, targeting LLP decays into electron-positron pairs. We observe no significant excess above the expected background and set 90% confidence-level upper limits on an effective production cross section at the level of $10^{-38}$ cm$^2$ for laboratory decay lengths of 0.3-100 m. These results complement existing searches by probing displaced decay signatures at meter-scale decay lengths.
papers.reason: First search for long-lived particles using the SBND Cosmic Ray Tagger beam telescope data, perfectly aligned with short-baseline BSM searches. [favorite author: Pedro Machado]

summary.tldr: Uses the standalone SBND Cosmic Ray Tagger Beam Telescope data ($2.95\times 10^{20}$ POT) to set 90% CL limits ($\sigma \sim 10^{-38}\text{ cm}^2$) on long-lived particles from neutrino upscattering.
summary.novel_idea: Performs the first BSM search using SBND data, utilizing a standalone pre-installation deployment of Cosmic Ray Tagger (CRT) panels as a 9.26-m decay volume telescope. It specifically targets long-lived particles (LLPs) produced via neutrino upscattering in upstream dirt/shielding that decay into $e^+e^-$ pairs in flight.
summary.method: Analyzed $2.95\times 10^{20}$ POT BNB data using an upstream panel veto, a two-hit requirement on the downstream panel, and a minimum spatial separation cut (>22 cm). BDTs trained on hit position, timing, and energy deposition discriminated signal from GENIE/Geant4-simulated neutrino backgrounds and data-driven pre-spill cosmics across lab decay lengths from 0.3 to 100 m.
key_results: Observed no significant excess in high-BDT score regions across tested decay lengths (p-values 0.65 to 0.86).

Excluded effective production cross sections $\sigma(\nu A \to NX) \times \mathrm{Br}(N \to e^+e^- + E_{\mathrm{miss}})$ down to $\sim 5\times 10^{-39}\text{ cm}^2$ at 90% CL for meter-scale decay lengths.
Probes parameter space of $3+2$ dark neutrino models with mass splittings $\Delta \sim 20\%$ that are unconstrained by prompt decay searches.
summary.why_it_matters: Relevant to BSM neutrino physics, specifically heavy neutral leptons, dark neutrinos, dipole portals, and upscattering signatures at SBN and DUNE Near Detector.
summary.caveats: Signal sensitivity is limited by single-hit dominance in the downstream CRT due to geometric acceptance and lack of magnetic tracking or particle identification in the standalone CRT configuration.

papers.title: Beta decay of potassium-54 reveals the role of two-body currents in neutron-rich nuclei
papers.abstract: The beta decay of neutron-rich nuclei probes the microscopic nature of weak interactions in the nuclear medium under extreme conditions. Such weak decays drive the synthesis of heavy elements in astrophysical environments, but remain poorly understood. Far from stability, experimental data are scarce, placing strong demands on ab initio nuclear theory. Two-body weak currents have been proposed as the dominant mechanism responsible for the universal quenching of theoretically predicted Gamow-Teller decay strength. However, direct experimental validation in neutron-rich nuclei has been lacking. Here we measure the beta decay of 54K, a nucleus at the experimental frontier of radioactive ion-beam facilities. In this work, the doubly magic nature of the daughter nucleus 54Ca results in a remarkably simple decay pattern, dominated by a single transition to a neutron-unbound state at 6.2 MeV with a comparative partial half-life logft=4.4(1) or Gamow-Teller decay strength B(GT)=0.26 (+0.08) (-0.04). Our measurement is reproduced by new state-of-the-art calculations of the decay, providing direct evidence for the essential role of two-body currents in nuclear beta decay for systems with a significant neutron excess. We establish a key benchmark for theoretical predictions of weak processes in exotic nuclei.
papers.reason: Measures beta decay of K-54 and provides direct experimental evidence for the role of two-body weak currents in neutron-rich nuclei, perfectly in core nuclear/neutrino physics.

summary.tldr: Measures $^{54}\text{K}$ $\beta$-decay at FRIB, revealing a single GT transition to a 6.16 MeV state in $^{54}\text{Ca}$ that provides direct experimental proof of two-body weak current quenching in neutron-rich nuclei.
summary.novel_idea: Presents the first detailed $\beta$-decay spectroscopy of exotic $^{54}\text{K}$ ($N=35, Z=19$), observing a remarkably clean single Gamow-Teller transition across a large neutron excess. Benchmarks state-of-the-art ab initio VS-IMSRG calculations in a multi-shell valence space ($sd$-$pf$ cross-shell), providing direct evidence for two-body weak current quenching far from stability.
summary.method: Implanted $\sim 4600$ $^{54}\text{K}$ ions into a YSO detector at the FRIB Decay Station initiator (FDSi), measuring $\beta$-delayed $\gamma$-rays (DEGAi clovers) and time-of-flight neutrons (VANDLE). Conducted ab initio VS-IMSRG and coupled-cluster calculations using the chiral 1.8/2.0(EM) NN+3N interaction in an $sd$-$pf$ multi-shell valence space, incorporating normal-ordered two-body weak currents (2BCs).
key_results: Discovered dominant $\beta$-feeding ($59\pm 8\%$) to a neutron-unbound state at 6159(100) keV in $^{54}\text{Ca}$, yielding $\log ft = 4.4(1)$ and $B(\mathrm{GT}) = 0.26^{+0.08}_{-0.04}$.
VS-IMSRG calculations predict $B(\mathrm{GT}) = 0.25$ ($3^-$ initial state) and $0.14$ ($4^-$ initial state) with 2BCs, compared to $0.43$ and $0.35$ without 2BCs.
Demonstrates that chiral two-body currents naturally account for the ~50% Gamow-Teller strength quenching in strongly neutron-rich systems without ad hoc $g_A$ quenching.
summary.why_it_matters: Crucial benchmark for ab initio nuclear theory, electroweak response, and lattice/chiral EFT two-body weak currents (2BC), directly impacting neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling, CEvNS nuclear matrix elements, and $r$-process $\beta$-decay inputs.
summary.caveats: VS-IMSRG in the truncations used overpredicts the excitation energy of the GT state (7.4 MeV vs 6.16 MeV experimental) due to VS-IMSRG(2) spectrum expansion, though the integrated GT matrix element remains robust.

papers.title: Phase-Twist Instability in a Coprecessing Neutrino Plasma
papers.abstract: Dense neutrino plasmas support collective flavor motion. We derive the first explicit dispersion relation about a flavor-nondiagonal background, focusing on the coprecession solution underlying spectral-split formation during the prompt neutrino burst of an electron-capture supernova. We show that slow phase modulations are unstable Goldstone modes, causing the coprecession plane to wobble with increasing amplitude. The instability emerges in the hydrodynamic limit, governed by conservation laws and without resolving flavor-precession resonances. Coprecessing neutrino plasmas resemble magnetized plasmas: a coherent flavor field drives flavor isospins to precess, and the phase-twist instability is the flavor analog of the firehose instability.
papers.reason: Derives the dispersion relation and phase-twist instability for dense coprecessing neutrino plasmas in supernovae, directly aligning with collective neutrino oscillations.

summary.tldr: Derives the first explicit dispersion relation for perturbations about a flavor-nondiagonal coprecessing neutrino plasma, identifying a generic hydrodynamic Goldstone instability analogous to the firehose instability of magnetized plasmas.
summary.novel_idea: Extends collective neutrino flavor stability theory from standard flavor-diagonal states to a self-consistent flavor-nondiagonal coprecessing background, which underpins spectral-split formation during electron-capture supernova $\nu_e$ bursts. It proves that one-sided coprecessions maximize corotating flavor energy, making slow phase modulations of the coprecession plane unstable Goldstone modes that grow in the hydrodynamic limit governed purely by lepton-number conservation.
summary.method: The authors formulate 1D mean-field kinetic equations in the mass basis within a corotating frame for two neutrino flavors. They solve the continuity equation for small spacetime phase modulations $\delta\Phi$ to extract a quadratic hydrodynamic dispersion relation, mapping the tensor structure to superfluid stiffness. They further linearize kinetic equations to construct the full flavor susceptibility, demonstrating that Cherenkov resonances map into cyclotron resonances where particle comoving frequencies match local flavor-precession frequencies.
key_results: Proves that all one-sided coprecession configurations ($\alpha_{\mathbf{p}} > 0$) have an elliptic dispersion relation yielding an unstable Goldstone branch with $\gamma = \mathrm{Im}(\omega) \propto k$ at low $k$.

Demonstrates parametric scaling of the hydrodynamic growth rate as $\mathrm{Im}(u_+) \sim \Delta v \Delta\theta$, requiring both non-zero angular spread $\Delta v$ and flavor-isospin misalignment $\Delta\theta$.

Shows kinetic stabilization occurs at $k \sim |\vec{H}_{\mathbf{p}}| \Delta\theta / \Delta v$, yielding a maximum instability rate $\gamma_{\max} \sim |\vec{H}_{\mathbf{p}}| \Delta\theta^2$ (or $\gamma \sim w_{\mathbf{p}}^2/\mu$ for small vacuum splittings $w_{\mathbf{p}} \ll \mu$).
Establishes a formal plasma analogy where the wobbling coprecession plane mirrors magnetic field buckling in the firehose instability.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts core-collapse and electron-capture supernova neutrino emission modeling. The onset of this instability before spectral splits fully develop will alter the emergent $\nu_e$ and $\bar{\nu}_e$ spectra, impacting predicted detection rates and pointing capabilities for DUNE, Hyper-K, and low-energy stopped-pion or CEvNS programs.
summary.caveats: Restricted to two-flavor, one-dimensional axially symmetric systems neglecting antineutrinos, and assumes an initially homogeneous coprecession background.

papers.title: Global Analysis of Nuclear Parton Distribution Functions using Markov Chain Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Global analyses of nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) have traditionally used the Hessian method for uncertainty estimation, relying on a local quadratic approximation of the chi-squared function. This Gaussian approximation can be inadequate when experimental constraints are limited and parameter correlations are strong, as it cannot fully capture asymmetric uncertainties, flat directions, or multiple minima. This thesis develops a Bayesian framework for nPDF determination using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) techniques within the nCTEQ analysis framework. An adaptive Metropolis-Hastings algorithm enables direct sampling of the posterior distribution, revealing pronounced non-Gaussian behavior and secondary minima, particularly in the valence distributions. The analysis presents the first global single-nucleus determination of lead (Pb) PDFs based exclusively on lead data, complemented by a multi-nuclei analysis incorporating different nuclear targets through a standard analytic dependence on the mass number. Including lighter nuclei significantly constrains quark distributions and changes the extracted lead PDFs, while the gluon distribution remains comparatively stable. A comparison with Hessian-based results highlights the limitations of the Gaussian approximation in regions with strong nonlinearity or multimodality. Overall, this work establishes Bayesian MCMC inference as a flexible framework for nPDF determination, providing a more comprehensive characterization of parameter uncertainties and the underlying parameter space.
papers.reason: Performs a global analysis of nuclear parton distribution functions using Bayesian MCMC within the nCTEQ framework, overcoming Hessian limitations.

summary.tldr: Develops a Bayesian MCMC framework within nCTEQ for nuclear PDFs, presenting the first single-nucleus Pb-only global fit and demonstrating significant non-Gaussianities and multimodality missed by Hessian analyses.
summary.novel_idea: Implements the first fully Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo global analysis of nuclear parton distribution functions within the nCTEQ framework, replacing the standard quadratic Hessian $\chi^2$ approximation. It delivers the first single-nucleus global extraction of lead ($A=208$) PDFs relying solely on lead data, offering an empirical baseline to quantify parameterization biases introduced by standard $A$-dependent assumptions.
summary.method: Utilizes an adaptive Metropolis-Hastings MCMC sampling framework interfaced with DGLAP evolution and experimental datasets (deep-inelastic scattering, neutrino-nucleus DIS, Drell-Yan, and LHC $p\mathrm{Pb}$ vector boson/heavy flavor data). Chains are systematically monitored for thermalization and autocorrelation. Posterior distributions and credible intervals from the Pb-only analysis are evaluated against a global Multi-nuclei analysis and traditional Hessian fits.
key_results: The Pb-only MCMC analysis reveals significant non-Gaussian structures and multiple local minima in the valence quark sector (notably the $a_3$ parameter) that are hidden in standard Hessian fits.
Inclusion of multi-target nuclear data strongly regularizes the posterior landscape, eliminating multimodal valence ambiguities and improving the validity of Gaussian Hessian approximations.

Demonstrates that gluon distributions in lead remain comparatively stable between single-nucleus and multi-nuclei fits, while quark distributions shift appreciably when cross-nuclear data are included.
Constructs compressed, statistically validated LHAPDF replica representations directly from the sampled Bayesian posterior.
summary.why_it_matters: Highly relevant for neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling at high $Q^2$ (neutrino DIS and shallow-inelastic scattering). The treatment of neutrino-lead DIS data and the quantification of non-Gaussian PDF uncertainties directly feed into cross-section calculations for neutrino experiments like DUNE, FASER$\nu$, and forward physics facilities.
summary.caveats: Computational cost of MCMC sampling restricts the total parameter space dimensionality and necessitated excluding certain secondary nuclear datasets compared to standard Hessian releases.

papers.title: Effects of Short-Range Correlations on Quarkyonic Matter
papers.abstract: In this work, we focus on investigating the impact of the short-range correlations on the properties of quarkyonic matter. These correlations induce the scattering of nucleons to momenta exceeding the Fermi momentum, thereby altering the momentum-space occupation distribution that underlies the quarkyonic framework. In particular, we examine to what extent the emergence of a high-momentum tail, due to the short-range nucleon-nucleon correlations, in the momentum distribution, for momenta exceeding the Fermi momentum, affects the fundamental properties of quarkyonic matter, such as the energy density, pressure, and speed of sound, among others. In fact, at high densities, the behavior of the momentum distribution has been established, both experimentally and theoretically, to follow a characteristic $\sim 1/k^4$ dependence at large momenta. To the best of our knowledge, this effect on quarkyonic matter has not yet been systematically investigated. Moreover, this experimentally confirmed feature of the momentum distribution suggests that heavy-ion collisions may probe quarkyonic matter, underscoring the importance of incorporating short-range correlations into a complete quarkyonic model.
papers.reason: Investigates the impact of nucleon short-range correlations on quarkyonic matter and high-momentum tails, aligning directly with nuclear-theoretic interests.

summary.tldr: Incorporates nucleon short-range correlations with a high-momentum tail into two-flavor quarkyonic matter, finding slight high-density softening of the equation of state and increased neutron star radii at lower masses.
summary.novel_idea: Presents the first systematic investigation of nucleon short-range correlations (SRCs) within the quarkyonic matter framework. It accounts for high-momentum nucleon states above the Fermi surface ($k > k_{F_n}$) obeying the characteristic $\sim 1/k^4$ tail when evaluating the thermodynamic properties of dense matter.
summary.method: Modifies the pure neutron momentum distribution via a phenomenological ansatz that enforces a $1/k^4$ tail containing a fixed fraction of nucleons (set to $\chi_n^{\mathrm{HMT}} = 0.1$). Embeds this distribution into a chargeless, two-flavor ($u, d$) quarkyonic model where noninteracting quarks occupy the core Fermi sea ($k < k_{0n}$) and interacting neutrons occupy an outer shell ($k_{0n} \le k \le k_{F_n}$), subsequently solving the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) equations.
key_results: Finds that SRCs induce opposite effects in different phases: they stiffen the equation of state in pure neutron matter, but slightly soften it in quarkyonic matter.
Demonstrates that the speed of sound $c_s^2$ retains its characteristic quarkyonic peak at low densities with only minor shifts from the high-momentum tail.
Calculates that incorporating SRCs increases neutron star radii at lower stellar masses while leaving the maximum supported mass virtually unchanged.
summary.why_it_matters: Tangential to the reader's primary electroweak and neutrino-scattering program; while short-range correlations are a core nuclear structure interest, here they are applied strictly to macroscopic compact-star equation of state modeling rather than lepton-nucleus scattering dynamics.
summary.caveats: Uses an idealized chargeless two-flavor model without protons, electrons, or beta equilibrium, and fixes the high-momentum tail fraction to an ad-hoc constant value of 10%.

papers.title: Impact of Neutrino Trapping on the Equation of State and Structure of Hybrid Stars with 2SC Quark Matter
papers.abstract: We investigate how sensitive the effects of neutrino trapping on hot hybrid stars are to uncertainties in the hadronic and quark equations of state and in the thermodynamic construction of the hadron--quark transition. The hadronic phase is described by finite-temperature covariant density functional equations of state, and the quark phase by a three-flavor Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model with repulsive vector interactions and two-flavor color superconductivity. Because confinement is absent from the NJL model, an effective pressure shift $B^*$ is used phenomenologically to locate the deconfinement transition. We construct isentropic stellar equations of state with and without trapped electron neutrinos, vary the quark vector coupling and the nuclear symmetry-energy slope, and compare global with local conservation of electron-lepton number within phase coexistence. Neutrino trapping generically shifts deconfinement toward higher density throughout the parameter range considered. Increasing the vector interaction stiffens quark matter and raises the maximum stellar mass, but only moderately for the couplings studied. We also examine stronger diquark pairing and RG-consistent regularization, instead of sharp momentum cut-off: both affect the pairing gap, phase boundaries, and quark-core composition more strongly than they alter the qualitative trends of the stellar mass--radius sequences. Conversely, trapping reduces the sensitivity to the hadronic symmetry-energy slope because the enhanced proton fraction drives matter toward greater isospin symmetry. Global and local lepton-number prescriptions produce rather similar mass--radius relations but substantially different internal phase structures: global conservation leads to a considerably more extended mixed phase.
papers.reason: Examines the impact of neutrino trapping on hot hybrid stars and equations of state with quark matter, aligning closely with nuclear equation of state and supernova neutrino physics.

summary.tldr: Analyzes the sensitivity of hot 2SC hybrid star equations of state to neutrino trapping, showing that trapping robustly delays deconfinement and suppresses dependence on the nuclear symmetry energy slope.
summary.novel_idea: Conducts a comprehensive sensitivity study of how neutrino trapping alters the hadron-quark deconfinement transition across a broad microphysical parameter space. It demonstrates that neutrino trapping markedly decreases sensitivity to the hadronic symmetry energy slope and reveals that while global Gibbs versus local Maxwell lepton conservation yield nearly identical bulk mass-radius curves, they produce starkly different internal mixed-phase profiles.
summary.method: Employs finite-temperature covariant density functional theory (DDLS family, $L_{\mathrm{sym}} = 30, 50, 70$ MeV) for hadrons and a 3-flavor NJL model with 2SC color superconductivity and vector repulsion for quarks. Evaluates isentropic stellar profiles ($S/A = 1, 2$) under both neutrino-trapped ($Y_{Le} = 0.4$) and neutrino-free conditions, testing both conventional and RG-consistent NJL regularizations alongside Gibbs and Maxwell phase constructions.
key_results: Trapped electron neutrinos robustly shift the onset of deconfinement to higher baryon densities across all considered quark vector couplings ($\eta_V = 0.8\text{--}1.2$) and bag constants $B^*$.

Shows that neutrino trapping significantly suppresses variation from $L_{\mathrm{sym}}$, as high lepton fractions force greater isospin symmetry (higher proton fraction), diminishing symmetry energy contributions.

Reveals that global Gibbs lepton conservation yields a substantially broader spatial mixed-phase core inside massive stars compared to local Maxwell matching, despite producing almost indistinguishable static mass-radius relations.
RG-consistent regularization prevents unphysical suppression of 2SC pairing gaps at high chemical potential but has minimal impact on the macroscopic mass-radius sequence.
summary.why_it_matters: Primarily relevant to dense-matter astrophysics (proto-neutron stars and binary mergers). While neutrino trapping is central to supernova thermodynamics, the paper focuses on compact-star equation-of-state and TOV profiles rather than neutrino interaction cross sections or detector signals.
summary.caveats: Relies on a phenomenological bag pressure shift $B^*$ to model deconfinement, neglects muon neutrinos, and assumes uniform entropy-per-baryon and lepton fractions rather than dynamical radial transport profiles.

papers.title: A Correspondence Between Qubit- and Boson-Based Sensing Protocols
papers.abstract: Recent years have seen a surge of interest in adapting non-classical states to search for physics beyond the Standard Model, including both qubit- and boson-based systems. These two classes of systems are closely related through the Holstein--Primakoff transformation (HPT). In this work, we show that the HPT offers novel insights into inherently quantum-mechanical detection of new physics. We begin by discussing how the HPT can be used to unify certain existing qubit- and boson-based proposals in a single framework. We then show how it naturally reveals a novel generalization of GHZ states which offer superior performance for the detection of rare interactions. We demonstrate that these novel states can be readily prepared, and combine the coherent advantage of GHZ states with superior error rejection. Finally, we show that the HPT also reveals a natural extension of the Hamiltonian-Not-in-Lindblad-Span theorem for collections of bosonic modes.
papers.reason: Connects qubit and boson-based sensing protocols via the Holstein-Primakoff transformation, offering insights for quantum-enhanced BSM searches. [favorite author: Harnik]

summary.tldr: Uses the Holstein-Primakoff transformation to connect qubit and bosonic dark-matter sensors, introducing a GHZ-4 entangled state that retains Heisenberg-scaling sensitivity while actively rejecting single-qubit decay backgrounds.
summary.novel_idea: Applies the Holstein-Primakoff transformation (HPT) to map quantum sensing protocols between distinguishable qubit systems and continuous-variable bosonic modes. By mapping a 4-legged bosonic cat state across the HPT into the symmetric qubit subspace, the authors construct a novel 'GHZ-4' entangled state that retains near-Heisenberg sensitivity while providing modulo-4 error rejection against single-qubit decay noise.
summary.method: Exploits the exact embedding of the symmetric subspace of $N$ qubits into Fock space via the HPT, expanding near the equator of the Bloch sphere. Calculates the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) for rotation and displacement signal Hamiltonians under Lindblad noise channels, and maps the Hamiltonian-Not-in-Lindblad-Span (HNLS) theorem to $m$ bosonic modes with $n$ excitations.
key_results: Unifies sensitivity bounds: optimal QFI scales as $F_Q \propto m n$ for bosonic modes (where excitations $n$ and modes $m$ are independent) versus $F_Q \propto N^2$ for $N$ qubits due to strict particle-number conservation.

Demonstrates that the GHZ-4 state achieves $F_Q = (N^2 + N)/2$, accepting only a factor-of-2 sensitivity reduction relative to standard GHZ states while enabling complete discrimination against $M \to M - 1$ qubit decay errors.

Proves that for collections of bosonic modes, Heisenberg scaling $(\Delta g)^{-2} \propto m n T^2$ is achievable under noise if and only if the bosonic signal generator lies outside the Lindblad noise span.
Provides explicit quantum circuit blueprints using standard one-axis twisting or parity gates to prepare GHZ-4 states with $O(N)$ operations.
summary.why_it_matters: Co-authored by Roni Harnik. Provides a direct theoretical bridge between quantum information techniques (GHZ states, entanglement, quantum error mitigation) and precision dark matter / light mediator searches (dark photons, axion-like particles), offering concrete experimental protocols relevant to BSM detection programs.
summary.caveats: Experimental implementation relies on maintaining high-fidelity multi-qubit entanglement and fast readout without introducing dominant dephasing channels that circumvent the modulo-4 symmetry.

papers.title: Precision measurement of the $J/\psi\to\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-$ branching fraction and search for a new gauge boson $Z^{\prime}$ at BESIII
papers.abstract: We present a precision measurement of the branching fraction of the rare decay $J/\psi\to\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-$, and a search for a new gauge boson $Z^{\prime}$ that couples only to the second and third lepton generations, using a data sample of $(8998 \pm 39) \times 10^6$ $J/\psi$ events collected by the BESIII detector. The branching fraction of the $J/\psi\to\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-$ decay is measured to be $B(J/\psi\to\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-)=[0.91\pm0.04~{\rm (stat.)}\pm0.07~{\rm (syst.)}]\times 10^{-6}$, representing the most precise measurement to date and consistent with the theoretical prediction within one standard deviation. Additionally, we search for $CP$ asymmetry in the $J/\psi\to\mu^+\mu^-\mu^+\mu^-$ decay and determine the T-odd observable to be $A_T = [0.05\pm 0.04~{\rm (stat.)}\pm0.01~{\rm (syst.)}]$, which is consistent with $CP$ conservation. In the search for $J/\psi\to Z^{\prime}\mu^+\mu^-$ via $Z^{\prime}\to\mu^+\mu^-$, no significant $Z^{\prime}$ signal is observed in the $\mu^+\mu^-$ invariant mass region of $(0.212,~2.6)$~GeV$/c^2$, and we set upper limits on the ${\rm U}(1)_{L_{\mu}-L_{\tau}}$ model coupling constant $g^{\prime}$ ranging from 0.001 to 0.294 at the 90\% confidence level, which is comparable to the upper limits set by Belle II for $Z^{\prime}$ masses below $0.7$~GeV$/c^2$.
papers.reason: BESIII precision measurement of rare J/psi decays and search for U(1) L_mu - L_tau gauge bosons, directly touching BSM dark sector searches. [favorite author: Tao Han]

papers.title: An open EFT for dark matter searches with matter-wave interferometers
papers.abstract: Matter-wave interferometers (MWIs) are a genuine quantum probe of dark matter (DM), being sensitive to DM-induced phase shifts and loss of contrast. Treating the interferometer as an open quantum system and the dark sector as its environment, we derive an open EFT to study these signatures using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism. Starting from a microscopic theory, we derive the interferometer's effective action, which we then project onto the many-body worldline sectors relevant for atom interferometers and MWIs employing mesoscopic objects, i.e., composite-particle interferometers (CPIs). This construction clarifies the heavy-probe limit and organizes phase shifts and decoherence as distinct real-time components of the influence action: the retarded kernel controls the causal response of the environment, while the Keldysh kernel controls environmental fluctuations and hence loss of contrast. At leading order, these kernels reduce to: (i) DM bubble diagrams in the case of four-point interactions, and (ii) dressed in-medium mediator propagators in the case of long-range interactions, where the dressing is provided by the DM environment. Within this framework, we study the signatures of elastic spin-independent sub-GeV DM scattering off nucleons and find that: (i) owing to Bose enhancements below the DM wave-particle boundary, ambitious CPIs could probe Higgs-portal DM with mass below 1 eV in an unexplored region of model space; (ii) for DM coupled to nucleons via a light hadrophilic scalar, the DM background can drive the mediator's in-medium mass tachyonic over much of parameter space; outside these regions, CPIs could probe provide powerful probes of light DM.
papers.reason: Develops an open effective field theory using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism to study dark matter scattering and decoherence in matter-wave interferometers.

papers.title: Chebyshev-expanded covariant density functional from relativistic Brueckner theory
papers.abstract: We construct a density-dependent covariant energy density functional (CE-ME1) from full-Dirac-space relativistic Brueckner--Hartree--Fock (RBHF) self-energies and the corresponding equation of state. The space-like component $U_V$ is incorporated at the Fermi surface through reduced scalar and time-like self-energies, which are mapped onto local Hartree $\sigma$, $\omega$, $\delta$, and $\rho$ channels. The density-dependent couplings are represented by cubic Chebyshev polynomials over the density range $0.08\leq\rho\leq0.48~{\rm fm}^{-3}$. A constrained thermodynamic calibration uses 199 RBHF energy-per-particle values from published microscopic computations at six isospin asymmetries, while maintaining positive, monotonic couplings. The Bonn-A RBHF saturation point, incompressibility $K_\infty=258$ MeV, symmetry energy $J=33.1$ MeV, and slope $L=65.2$ MeV are reproduced. The predicted curvature $K_{\rm sym}=33$ MeV differs from the published RBHF value of $-67$ MeV, illustrating the derivative sensitivity of the local reduction. The combined energy RMS is $0.613$ MeV, measuring model discrepancy rather than statistical uncertainty. Uniform matter remains mechanically stable and causal above saturation within the calibrated range. In cold charge-neutral $npe\mu$ matter, CE-ME1 reasonably reproduces the interpolated RBHF pressure and proton fraction over most of the interval, although the pressure discrepancy increases near its upper edge. The DD-ME2 benchmark is stiffer and predicts a lower proton fraction at high density.
papers.reason: Constructs a covariant energy density functional from relativistic Brueckner-Hartree-Fock theory using Chebyshev polynomials, directly relevant for nuclear matter equations of state.

papers.title: Nucleon decays into three leptons plus a kaon
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate baryon-number-violating (BNV) nucleon decays into three leptons and a kaon within the framework of low-energy effective field theory (LEFT). We identify all kinematically allowed four-body decay modes involving a $K^+$ or $K^0$ meson and derive their decay widths induced by local dimension-9 operators in terms of the LEFT Wilson coefficients. These results are obtained by classifying the relevant operators, which contain three lepton and three quark fields, including one strange quark, according to their transformation properties under the chiral symmetry group, matching them onto chiral perturbation theory. By reanalyzing existing experimental data, we establish stringent bounds on the partial lifetimes of these four-body decay modes and derive corresponding constraints on the dimension-9 Wilson coefficients. Our results provide a convenient EFT framework for connecting the underlying BNV interactions to experimental searches for these exotic nucleon decays.
papers.reason: Systematically investigates baryon-number-violating nucleon decays into three leptons and a kaon using low-energy effective field theory and chiral perturbation theory matching.

papers.title: Non-linear effects in coherent photoproduction of heavy quarkonia off nuclei: Green's function formalism vs Balitsky-Kovchegov equation
papers.abstract: We present an analysis of QCD non-linear (NL) effects in the coherent photoproduction of charmonia off nuclei at high energies corresponding to future measurements at the LHC. For the first time, we confront the energy evolution of such effects within our rigorous Green's function (GF) formalism with results from Refs.~\cite{Cepila:2025ujv,Cepila:2024qge}, which are based on the solution of the leading-order (LO) and next-to-leading-order (NLO) Balitsky-Kovchegov (BK) evolution equations. We demonstrate a huge difference in the NL effects between these two formalisms, exhibiting a rather strong rise with photon energy. Our analysis shows that NLO calculations of the BK equation from Ref.~\cite{Cepila:2024qge} slow down the rate of the high-energy LO evolution of NL effects. Although these calculations reduce the differences between the GF and BK predictions, they still lead to a much stronger onset of leading-twist shadowing effects compared to the GF formalism. The BK equation in its present form cannot be applied to nuclear targets and thus requires a non-trivial modification that properly incorporates quantum coherence effects.
papers.reason: Compares QCD non-linear evolution in coherent photoproduction on nuclei between the Green's function formalism and the Balitsky-Kovchegov equation, highly relevant for nuclear shadowing models.

papers.title: Systematic calculations of \beta-delayed fission probabilities using a microscopic framework
papers.abstract: The process of $\beta$-delayed fission ($\beta$DF) consists of a mother nucleus $\beta$-decaying to different states of a daughter isotope, followed by fission of the latter with a probability that strongly depends on the energy of the states populated in the $\beta$ decay. Studying this process experimentally can be challenging due to the typically small $\beta$DF probabilities. The theoretical framework presented in this work was developed to globally characterise $\beta$DF probabilities. This approach uses energy density functional based models to obtain the necessary inputs for the final probabilities, which are obtained through the nuclear reaction code TALYS. Calculations were performed for all isotopes with an experimentally measured value of $\beta$DF probabilities. Following the optimisation of the theoretical framework to better reproduce known data, a global RMS deviation of about two orders of magnitude was achieved, an accuracy that can be used to identify promising cases for future experimental $\beta$DF studies.
papers.reason: Performs microscopic calculations of beta-delayed fission probabilities using TALYS and EDF models, highly relevant to nuclear data and decay.

papers.title: Probing new $C\!P$-violating sources in $\Lambda_b\to\Lambda_c\ell^-\bar\nu_\ell$
papers.abstract:
While baryonic $C\!P$ violation has been observed, its potential to reveal new physics beyond the sensitivity of mesonic decays remains an open question. We investigate this potential within semileptonic $b	o c\ell ar
u_\ell$ transitions by comparing the angular distributions of $\Lambda_b	o\Lambda_c(	o\Lambda\pi)\ell^- ar
u_\ell$ and $ ar B	o D^*(	o D\pi)\ell^- ar
u_\ell$ utilizing lattice-QCD form factors. We perform a global fit to $R(D^{(*)})$ alongside auxiliary $C\!P$-even measurements to delineate the phenomenologically viable parameter space for new-physics Wilson coefficients. Leveraging these allowed ranges and the lattice inputs, we evaluate the complementary sensitivity of both angular distributions to novel weak phases. We demonstrate that the baryonic decay mode probes combinations of Wilson coefficients that remain inaccessible in mesonic angular distributions, thereby providing critical supplementary information for identifying new physics.
papers.reason: Investigates CP-violating sources and new physics in semileptonic Lambda_b decays using lattice-QCD form factors.

papers.title: Searches for new particle physics by methods of classical and neutrino astronomy
papers.abstract: Selected astrophysical methods for testing particle-physics models are reviewed. Stellar structure and evolution constrain additional channels of energy loss and transport; high-energy photon propagation probes photon mixing with new particles and modifications of electron-positron pair production; large-volume neutrino telescopes are used to search for magnetic monopoles, neutrinos from superheavy dark-matter decay, and non-standard neutrino propagation. Recent applications of these methods are discussed, involving the tip of the red-giant branch in the color-luminosity diagram, gamma-ray burst 221009A, and data from the Baikal Gigaton Volume Detector (Baikal-GVD) and the IceCube experiment. In each case, particle-physics parameters are inferred through a forward model that accounts for the response to new physics, propagation, detection, and nuisance parameters.
papers.reason: Reviews searches for new particle physics using stellar evolution, photon propagation, and neutrino telescopes like IceCube and Baikal-GVD.

papers.title: On-shell reduction of spin-zero Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau covariants and implications for the relativistic impulse approximation
papers.abstract: We analyze the on-shell content of the local Lorentz covariants of the five-dimensional spin-zero Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau algebra in elastic spin-zero-spin-$1/2$ scattering. The scalar, vector, and tensor structures are reduced explicitly to the two independent amplitudes allowed by the physical parity-conserving process. The two scalar structures are proportional on shell, the genuine nonminimal vector $i[P,\beta^\mu]$ is longitudinal and vanishes after contraction with the conserved fermion vector current, and the projected vectors $P\beta^\mu$ and $\beta^\mu P$ each reduce to one half of the minimal-vector contribution. The tensor covariants introduce no additional on-shell directions. We discuss the consequences for the four invariant choices used in meson-nucleus optical-potential calculations and show that different nuclear equations can arise only after on-shell-equivalent representatives are promoted to optical operators and iterated beyond the order at which the elementary impulse approximation is fixed. These results provide a systematic basis for distinguishing genuinely independent elementary amplitudes from representation-dependent effects generated by the optical embedding.
papers.reason: Analyzes on-shell reduction of DKP covariants in spin-0 and spin-1/2 elastic scattering and implications for relativistic optical potentials.

papers.title: Cosmic-string calorimetry with a 220\,PeV neutrino
papers.abstract: KM3NeT has reported KM3-230213A, a $220$\,PeV neutrino with no source identified. If it comes from a cosmic-string network, energy conservation makes the event a calorimeter. The flux measures the power the network has spent, not how it emits, and a cusp at critical current can supply that power at unit efficiency. The event gives $G\mu\epsilon_p=(2.8\text{--}4.3)\times10^{-11}$ for $f_\nu=0.1$. Pulsar timing already reaches $10^{-10}$, so one event competes with the arrays. For the branch that still radiates gravitationally, flux and timing together require a third of the network's energy in particles, a share that further events above $100$\,PeV would measure.
papers.reason: Interprets high-energy KM3NeT PeV neutrino events as cosmic-string calorimeters, connecting high-energy neutrinos to topological defects.

papers.title: Covariant Wigner function and spin polarization of the Rarita-Schwinger field
papers.abstract: We study the covariant Wigner function for the spin-$3/2$ Rarita-Schwinger field and its relation to the spin density matrix and the mean spin polarization vector. We obtain a formula relating the covariant Wigner function to the mean spin vector for a weakly interacting field. We then calculate the mean spin vector induced by thermal vorticity, thermal shear, and spin potential at local thermal equilibrium in the Belinfante, canonical and GLW pseudo-gauges. The resulting formula can be used to predict the spin polarization of spin-$3/2$ hadrons, such as the $\Omega^-$, in heavy-ion collisions. Differences in the thermal-shear induced polarization in the canonical and Belinfante pseudo-gauges make it possible to use local spin polarization measurements of the $\Omega^-$ to discriminate between the two pseudo-gauges.
papers.reason: Derives the covariant Wigner function and spin polarization for spin-3/2 Rarita-Schwinger fields, relevant to spin observables in nuclear collisions.

papers.title: Evidence of partonic collectivity in OO collisions through the measurement of $\phi$, K$^0_{\rm S}$, and $\Lambda$ elliptic flow
papers.abstract: The first measurement of the elliptic-flow coefficient ($v_{2}$) of $\phi$, K$^0_{\rm S}$, and $\Lambda (\overline{\Lambda})$ hadrons performed in OO collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.36$ TeV with the ALICE detector is presented as a function of transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) in central and semi-central collisions. For the $\phi$ meson, in particular, this is the first measurement of the elliptic flow in a small collision system. At low $p_{\rm T}$, a characteristic mass ordering of $v_{2}$ is observed, consistent with collective expansion of the system, in which heavier hadrons are shifted to higher $p_{\rm T}$ by a common velocity field. At intermediate $p_{\rm T}$, above 3 GeV/$c$, a baryon$-$meson splitting with a $10\sigma$ significance emerges, with the $\Lambda (\overline{\Lambda})$ baryon exhibiting larger $v_{2}$ values than mesons, while, despite its mass being close to the mass of the $\Lambda$, the $\phi$ follows the K$^{0}_{\rm S}$. The $\phi$ meson behavior disfavors a purely mass-driven interpretation of the observed patterns and supports the role of hadronization via quark recombination from a collectively flowing partonic medium. These results provide complementary evidence that key signatures of partonic collectivity observed in Pb$-$Pb collisions persist in light nucleus$-$nucleus systems.
papers.reason: ALICE measurement of elliptic flow in oxygen-oxygen collisions showing evidence of partonic collectivity and quark recombination in small systems.

papers.title: Measurement of antideuteron and net-$\Lambda$ number fluctuations at the Large Hadron Collider
papers.abstract: The recent measurements of event-by-event correlations between the antideuteron and antiproton numbers in Pb$-$Pb collisions at the LHC deviate from the statistical hadronization model parameterizations that describe the yields and fluctuations of light-flavored hadrons. This discrepancy may stem from nucleosynthesis processes involved in the formation of composite states like antideuterons. In this letter, we present the first measurement of the antideuteron$-$net-$\Lambda$ number correlation obtained in Pb$-$Pb collisions with the ALICE detector. This quantity is mostly sensitive to the quantum-number correlations induced by the hadronization process, as $\Lambda$ hyperons are not constituents of antideuterons. Both the antideuteron$-$net-$\Lambda$ number correlation and the normalized second-order cumulant of the net-$\Lambda$ number are well described by the statistical hadronization model implemented in Thermal-FIST. This establishes strong evidence that the antideuteron$-$antiproton correlation is driven by the nucleosynthesis processes, while the correlation between antideuterons and non-nucleonic hadrons is primarily sensitive to the hadronization mechanism.
papers.reason: ALICE measurement of antideuteron-net-Lambda correlations in Pb-Pb collisions, highlighting nucleosynthesis versus statistical hadronization mechanisms.

papers.title: Nuclear Data Evaluation Utilizing Bayesian Monte Carlo Methods
papers.abstract: While the body of experimental nuclear data continues to grow at a rapid pace, significant gaps persist. The lack of evaluated experimental data is far more pronounced in charged-particle reactions which are essential to a large portion of the isotope production community for vital medical, industrial, and national security interests. In the absence of experimental and evaluated data, isotope production relies on theoretical models that may result in low yield and isotopic impurities. This work investigates model and parameter adjustments in TALYS 2.0 to establish uncertainty bands on proton-induced cross sections, highlight influential parameters in calculations, and constrain adjustments within physically defensible bounds. The EXFOR dataset for proton-induced reactions on natural copper, comprised of 24 independent cross sections, was used for iterative Bayesian model updating. Upon convergence, parameters and their uncertainties were compared against 23 cumulative cross sections from EXFOR, highlighting the limitations of generalization. Various machine learning models were leveraged to predict TALYS performance, with a small neural network showing useful ranking capabilities across several generations, suggesting the use of a surrogate approach to screening for future evaluations.
papers.reason: Performs nuclear data evaluation and iterative Bayesian model updating using TALYS for proton-induced cross sections.

papers.title: Probing the inner disk edge of rotating neutron stars with dipole excitations in finite nuclei
papers.abstract: The nuclear equation of state shapes both the structure of rapidly rotating neutron stars and the orbital motion in their surrounding spacetime. Its uncertainty affects the mass and radius at which the innermost stable circular orbit reaches the stellar surface, a condition that defines the transition between disks whose inner edge is set by the surface and those truncated by orbital instability. We quantify how measurements of the electric dipole polarizability of neutron-rich nuclei reduce the uncertainty in this transition and in the orbital properties at the disk inner edge. We compute uniformly rotating neutron stars in general relativity for a family of equations of state that systematically vary the symmetry energy, derived from relativistic energy density functionals with density-dependent point-coupling interactions. We compare the results for the full family with those for the subset consistent with the measured dipole polarizabilities of finite nuclei. The dipole polarizability constraint reduces the spread in transition mass and equatorial radius by factors of about seven to ten across the spin frequencies considered. Along this transition, it also confines the orbital frequency at the disk inner edge to a band narrower than $20$~Hz at each spin. Combined with a measured neutron-star spin, a kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillation interpreted as disk orbital motion further restricts the mass--radius region, allowing an independent mass estimate to probe the symmetry-energy constraint. The dipole response of finite nuclei thus informs both the structure of rotating neutron stars and the orbital properties of their inner accretion disks.
papers.reason: Quantifies how electric dipole polarizability measurements in finite nuclei constrain neutron-star radii and disk edges, tightly connected to low-energy nuclear probes.

papers.title: Search for $e^{+}e^{-} \to \pi^0 K^+K^-J/\psi$ at $\sqrt{s}= 4.26 \sim$ 4.95 GeV
papers.abstract: Using $e^+e^-$ collision data collected with the BESIII detector at 27 center-of-mass energies between 4.26 and 4.95 GeV corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of $13.0~\text{fb}^{-1}$, we report the first search for the process $e^{+}e^{-} \to \pi^0 K^+K^-J/\psi$. We additionally probe the cross section spectra for potential charmonium-like vector states and invariant mass distributions for intermediate $Z_c/Z_{cs}$ state signals, and find no resonant structures consistent with these exotic candidates. Given the absence of observed resonant signals, upper limits at the 90\% confidence level are determined for the Born cross sections, along with their best-fit values, as well as for the production of the intermediate states.
papers.reason: Reports searches for $e^+e^-$ exotic meson and charmonium-like vector states with BESIII data. [favorite author: Tao Han]

papers.title: Late reheating in the era of precision cosmology
papers.abstract: We study the minimum cosmic reheating temperature allowed by recent measurements of primordial nuclear abundances and of the cosmic microwave background. We find that reheating by decays of a light particle into electrons and neutrinos is compatible with both at temperatures around 0.4 MeV, an order of magnitude below the bound for purely electromagnetic channels. This scenario has implications for cosmology and laboratory searches. For example, nearly standard neutrino radiation can coexist with a smaller active neutrino mass density at unchanged physical masses, by up to a factor of five for normal ordering. The weaker suppression of clustering changes matter power at the percent level, which forthcoming galaxy surveys and lensing measurements may probe. Late reheating also suppresses sterile neutrino production at mixings within the projected reach of laboratory experiments.
papers.reason: Studies minimum cosmic reheating temperatures via particle decays into electrons and neutrinos, exploring impacts on active neutrino mass density and cosmology.

papers.title: Quark Saturation in Magnetized Pure Neutron Matter
papers.abstract: We study how magnetic fields affect the onset of quark saturation, which limits the domain of applicability of a purely baryonic description. We consider matter composed of electrically neutral $ddu$ baryons, including neutron- and $\Delta^0$-like states. Using a simple constituent-quark model, we compute the baryon wave functions and spectra in magnetic fields. The magnetic field polarizes the spin-flavor structure, compresses the internal wave function in the transverse direction, and strongly suppresses the transverse kinetic energy. From the baryon wave functions, we construct the one-body reduced density matrix and derive the corresponding single-quark distributions in longitudinal momentum and Landau-level space. We then use these distributions to evaluate quark occupation probabilities in an ideal baryon gas and determine the onset of quark saturation. At finite magnetic field in the $+z$-direction, the $d_\downarrow$ quark in the lowest Landau level reaches saturation first. The resulting saturation density depends nonmonotonically on the magnetic-field strength: it decreases at weak fields and increases at stronger fields. This behavior reflects the competition between spin-flavor polarization, which promotes saturation, and transverse spatial squeezing, which delays saturation by broadening of the quark transverse momentum distribution.
papers.reason: Studies the effects of magnetic fields on quark saturation and baryon-to-quark transitions in magnetized neutron matter equations of state.

papers.title: The Disordered Universe 2025: Open Effective Field Theories
papers.abstract: Effective field theories (EFTs) offer a powerful method to unify diverse models under a small set of control parameters, allowing systematic expansions around well-established theories. While these techniques were traditionally developed for particle physics experiments with clean, isolated initial states, realistic macroscopic environments are often noisy and dissipative. Recognising the limitations of traditional EFTs has recently sparked intense progress at the interface of high-energy physics and condensed matter. These developments motivate a new approach to gravitation and cosmology, one that models the gravitational sector as evolving in the presence of an unobservable medium. Open Effective Field Theories provide a systematic, controllable framework for this endeavour. This chapter presents this versatile framework and illustrates how the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism captures the influence of unknown environments, manifesting as dissipation and noise, on observational probes. These notes are based on a series of lectures held during the La Ricotta Summer School "The Disordered Universe 2025" from 21 July to 1 August 2025.
papers.reason: Pedagogical lectures on Open Effective Field Theories and the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, directly applicable to open quantum system treatments of neutrino and dark matter decoherence.

papers.title: Quasiparticle Modeling of Strange Quark Stars with In-Medium QCD Effects at Finite Temperature and Strong Magnetic Fields
papers.abstract: This work investigates the properties of spin polarized strange quark matter SQM and the resulting structure of strange quark stars SQSs within a thermodynamically self consistent quasiparticle framework. By developing a dynamic bag constant intrinsically coupled to the medium dependent reduction of quark effective masses we ensure strict internal thermodynamic consistency. This coupling gives rise to a distinct non monotonic behavior in the speed of sound significantly stiffening the Equation of State EoS at high densities. Consequently our model predicts maximum stable gravitational masses up to 2.19 Mo. These results demonstrate that hot magnetized SQM provides a robust and viable mechanism to explain ultra massive pulsars such as PSR J0740 6620 and PSR J0952 0607 without requiring unrealistic thermal or structural assumptions.
papers.reason: Models strange quark matter and pulsar equations of state at finite temperature and magnetic fields using a thermodynamically consistent quasiparticle framework.

papers.title: What the Primary Lund Plane Omits: A Model-Stitching Diagnosis of a Jet-Tagger Representation Gap
papers.abstract: Lund-plane and Particle Transformer (ParT) jet taggers can differ in performance because one representation is weaker, or because a weaker downstream computation reads an adequate one. Standalone performance cannot separate these. Model stitching can: it links the frozen early layers of one network to the frozen late layers of another through a single trained linear map. As a positive control we use an incomplete Lund representation, the primary declustering branch, whose deficit is known independently. Stitched into ParT's downstream, it reaches a background rejection at least as much as its own downstream recovers, yet far below ParT's background rejection: the deficit is representational, not computational. A hypergraph reader over splitting triplets does no better, ruling out higher-order correlations as the cause. The gap is invisible in AUC, which stays within 1\% of its target value, and appears only in background rejection at low signal efficiency. It localizes to 0.6\% of background jets, at and above the top mass, with more constituents but fewer primary splittings than typical background. Rebuilding the representation on the full Cambridge/Aachen declustering tree repairs the deficit as predicted: standalone rejection rises, closing 72\% of the gap. Masking nodes at inference shows the repaired network still relies almost entirely on the primary branch; the secondary splittings make the representation learnable rather than supplying information it reads. Along the primary branch, the widest-angle splitting, near the top and $W$ opening angles, is worth nearly twice a random one. For quark/gluon tagging the primary branch is far less deficient, retaining 77.6\% of ParT's rejection (46.9\% for top), and the full tree closes only 33\% of the gap (72\% for top).
papers.reason: Diagnoses representation gaps in Lund-plane and transformer jet taggers using model stitching, relevant to QCD tools in high-energy physics.

papers.title: On-shell Mass Renormalisation and RG-improved Effective Potential in Vector-like Lepton Models
papers.abstract: We discuss the on-shell mass renormalisation in a class of six vector-like lepton (VLL) extensions of the Standard Model with seesaw-like contributions to the SM lepton masses. The schemes absorb large radiative corrections to the SM lepton masses arising from mixing between the SM and VLLs with up to $5\times5$ mixing matrices and allows for efficient computation of observables and the low-scale $\overline{\text{MS}}$ values of model parameters. We determine and solve the redundancy-free 2-loop renormalisation-group (RG) equations, compute the RG-improved effective potential and study the vacuum instability scales of each of the VLL models. We find rich phase behaviour and parameter regions that show instability scales as low as $10^5$ GeV as well as regions where the one-loop corrections to the input parameters can lead to a stable vacuum.
papers.reason: Investigates on-shell mass renormalization and RG-improved effective potentials in vector-like lepton models with seesaw mechanisms.

papers.title: Subpercent accuracy in molecular electric quadrupole coupling: nuclear-size and relativistic effects in RaF
papers.abstract: We report a benchmark study of the electric-quadrupole hyperfine interaction in the electronic ground state of the RaF molecule, including finite-nuclear-size effects. The calculations include relativistic effects using the Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonian and electron correlation up to perturbative quadruple excitations within the coupled cluster framework. At the achieved level of accuracy, penetration of the electronic density into the finite nuclear quadrupole distribution produces a non-negligible correction to the usual electric field gradient (EFG) description at the center of the nucleus and must be considered. At a fixed rms charge radius, the EFG is much less sensitive to the shape of the monopole nuclear charge distribution: electron wavefunctions computed using the Gaussian and Fermi nuclear charge models yield nearly identical EFGs. The recommended effective EFG parameter for the $X\,{}^{2}\Sigma_{1/2}$ electronic ground state is $\langle q\rangle_0=-5.178(21)$ a.u., with an estimated uncertainty reduced by an order of magnitude compared to previous studies. Combined with future measurements of electric-quadrupole hyperfine coupling constants in RaF, this result can be used to determine the nuclear quadrupole moments of Ra isotopes with record precision.
papers.reason: Performs high-precision calculations of nuclear-size and relativistic effects on electric quadrupole hyperfine interactions in RaF for isotope moments.

papers.title: Elastic Scattering of Dirac Dark Matter with Charged Leptons through a Scalar Mediator: Analytical Framework, Numerical Stability, and Direct-Detection Bounds
papers.abstract: We investigate a leptophilic simplified dark matter model in which a Dirac fermion \chi interacts with Standard Model charged leptons \ll through a real scalar mediator S. Starting from the low-energy Yukawa interaction Lagrangian in the fermion mass eigenbasis, we derive closed-form tree-level analytical expressions for the invariant scattering amplitude, the spin-averaged squared matrix element, and the differential and total elastic cross sections. To overcome the numerical loss of significance that arises when evaluating the standard antiderivative difference in the heavy-mediator regime, we rearrange the phase-space integral into positive-definite recoil contributions supplemented by convergent power-series expansions. This analytical formulation smoothly connects the light-mediator and heavy-mediator regimes without relying on Effective Field Theory (EFT) contact approximations, allowing us to establish quantitative validity criteria for the contact limit. Finally, we map the microscopic differential cross section onto the reference electron-scattering cross section and evaluate the resulting coupling constraints using experimental data from SENSEI, DAMIC, SuperCDMS, XENON10, and XENON1T.
papers.reason: Derives analytical cross sections and direct-detection bounds for elastic scattering of Dirac dark matter with charged leptons via a scalar mediator.

papers.title: Relativistic Elastic Scattering of Cosmic-Ray Boosted Dirac Dark Matter with Charged Leptons through a Scalar Mediator
papers.abstract: We investigate the relativistic kinematics, spinor-recoil structure, and direct-detection phenomenology of a Dirac dark matter fermion interacting with SM charged leptons through a real scalar mediator within a low-energy effective Lagrangian in the fermion mass basis. Standard halo direct-detection searches lose sensitivity for sub-MeV dark matter, because the maximum recoil energy falls below detector thresholds. When halo dark matter particles are upscattered to relativistic energies by galactic cosmic-ray electrons (CRE), the momentum transfer in both the astrophysical upscattering stage and the terrestrial detection stage can exceed the fermion mass scales. By decomposing the tree-level $t$-channel cross section into three positive-definite contributions, we separate the static-numerator contribution from the linear and quadratic momentum-transfer spinor-recoil contributions, evaluated via convergent power series that reduce subtractive cancellation at small momentum transfer. For incident large kinetic energies, the spinor-recoil contributions become comparable to and begin to exceed $\sigma_0$; at substantially higher energies, they enhance the total cross section by several orders of magnitude relative to the static-numerator approximation. Furthermore, retaining the dynamical scalar propagator yields a high-energy cross section that decreases as $1/s$ and satisfies $s$-wave helicity partial-wave unitarity, in contrast to the linear $\mathcal{O}(s/m_S^4)$ growth of the contact approximation. Applying the exact differential recoil spectra within an effective propagation model for cosmic-ray electron boosted dark matter (CRE-BDM), we derive $90\%$ C.L. exclusion bounds in the 1 keV -- 10 MeV mass range from Super-Kamiokande, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T, extending experimental sensitivity into the sub-MeV window.
papers.reason: Investigates relativistic kinematics and spinor-recoil structure for cosmic-ray boosted dark matter scattering on charged leptons.

papers.title: A Practical Guide to Sensitivity Projections for Beyond the Standard Model Physics
papers.abstract: Statistics is a well-established discipline, yet its application can be confusing, particularly in fields where the language of statistics is unfamiliar and when making projections, where real data is not yet available. Both of these factors are commonplace in Beyond the Standard Model physics. In this work, we clarify the distinction between goodness-of-fit tests, which assess the compatibility of an observation with a single hypothesis, and hypothesis tests, which quantify how strongly some data prefer one hypothesis over another. We emphasise that for Beyond the Standard Model sensitivity projections, hypothesis testing should be used. We give detailed examples using both Poisson and multinomially distributed data, deriving exact $p$-values and discussing Monte Carlo and asymptotic approximations. We further demonstrate that for the Asimov data set all the test statistics discussed, for both goodness-of-fit tests and hypothesis tests, can be approximated by Pearson's $\chi^2$ statistic, and the difference in approaches comes down to the distribution of the test statistics. We also compare goodness-of-fit and hypothesis test $p$-values in two realistic examples. We (1) consider the reach of a muon collider on heavy spin-1 resonances and (2) provide updated projections for the potential of current and future gamma ray telescopes to probe new dark sectors via the observation of Hawking radiation from the explosion of a black hole. Finally, we discuss the CLs method, the significance and systematic errors.
papers.reason: Clarifies statistical methods, hypothesis testing, and sensitivity projections for BSM physics searches.

papers.title: Dark Matter Coherent Freeze-Out Mechanism: A Comprehensive Analysis
papers.abstract: Both Weakly-Interacting Massive Particle (WIMP) and Axion-Like Particle (ALP) are attractive particle dark matter candidates. In this paper we consider a scenario in which both WIMP and ALP are present. The two species interact via a non-derivative quadratic coupling modeled on the axion-nucleon interaction in QCD. We show that even a small (Planck-suppressed) coupling can drastically modify the cosmological history of both species. In the very early Universe, the ALP field acquires a vacuum expectation value, and the system undergoes an inverse phase transition at a temperature around or below the weak scale. WIMPs may remain in equilibrium far beyond the usual freeze-out time, eventually decoupling via a novel "coherent freeze-out" mechanism. WIMP annihilation cross sections several orders of magnitude above the canonical thermal target value can be consistent with the observed relic density in the coherent freeze-out scenario. At the same time, coherent oscillations of the ALP field do not begin until after the phase transition, and the initial conditions for these oscillations are set by the thermal physics of the phase transition. The ALP relic density is then predicted unambiguously in terms of the WIMP mass and coupling. We term this scenario "ALP miracle", since the observed relic density is obtained when these parameters are around their natural values, the weak and the Planck scale. The ALP miracle scenario prefers the ALP mass above about $10^{-3}\,\mathrm{eV}$, far larger than other popular ALP dark matter models. The ALP miracle parameter space overlaps with a currently allowed region of the QCD axion band, a large fraction of which is expected to be probed by the proposed IAXO experiment.
papers.reason: Analyzes a joint WIMP and axion-like particle scenario featuring a novel coherent freeze-out mechanism modifying relic abundance calculations.

papers.title: Hybrid seesaw from $SU(2)_1 \times SU(2)_2 \times U(1)_Y$
papers.abstract: We study neutrino mass generation in a model based on the $SU(3)_c \times SU(2)_1 \times SU(2)_2 \times U(1)_Y$ gauge symmetry, in which the Standard Model $SU(2)_L$ arises at low energies as the diagonal subgroup of the two $SU(2)$ factors. The symmetry is enlarged with a global $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry, spontaneously broken by the vacuum expectation value of a scalar bidoublet. Light neutrino masses are generated at tree level through a hybrid of the type-III, inverse and linear seesaw mechanisms. A distinctive feature of the construction is the existence of a Nambu-Goldstone boson, the majoron, which transforms non-trivially under the original gauge symmetry while being mostly singlet under the Standard Model gauge group. We explore the phenomenological consequences of this setup, including electroweak precision constraints, the production of the nearly degenerate $W'$ and $Z'$ bosons at colliders and lepton flavor violating decays with a majoron in the final state. The latter constitute the most promising signature of the model.
papers.reason: Constructs a neutrino mass model featuring a hybrid of type-III, inverse, and linear seesaw mechanisms with a viable majoron.

papers.title: Side jump and anomalous Lorentz transformation of a coherent Dirac wave packet
